description: Protocol/Evidence Advisor knowledge base — 8 evidence-backed rules (P1-P8) + normalization rules (N1-N4). Each rule has citation DOIs. Descriptive only: match scores are not prescriptive.

rules.title: SYBR + high family cross-reactivity
rules.recommendation: A seed-family member is at high or identical cross-reactivity risk for this assay. In stem-loop RT-qPCR, members that differ near the 3′ end are told apart mainly at the RT step, by the stem-loop primer and its 3′ overhang, not by the detection chemistry (Chen et al. 2005); SYBR Green reports every amplified product and adds no discrimination of its own. Test the assay on synthetic templates of the close family members; if the cross-signal is too high, design a separate stem-loop RT primer for each member or use a probe-based (TaqMan) assay.
pros: A probe assay gives no signal from primer-dimers or unrelated products (it does not by itself separate family members)
A separate RT primer per member can improve discrimination; confirm it on synthetic templates
cons: TaqMan probes add cost
Multiple RT reactions increase workload

sources.note: let-7 panel; members differ by 1 nt; SYBR required stringent annealing optimisation
original stem-loop RT-qPCR; specificity derives from stem-loop steric hindrance, not probe

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: Difficult sample type or low input RNA
rules.recommendation: Consider LNA-enhanced primers: literature reports improved accuracy and reproducibility at low RNA input (FFPE, plasma) compared to standard DNA primers.
pros: Improved Tm and hybridisation affinity for short miRNA targets [Andreasen10]
Reliable down to ~20 copies per reaction [Kunwar23]
Reported for low-input clinical RNA [Andreasen10]; check on your own sample type
cons: LNA oligo synthesis cost is higher than standard DNA
Require empirical Tm optimisation
Limited to research use without clinical validation

sources.note: LNA-enhanced primer improved quantification in total RNA from clinical samples
stem-loop TaqMan vs LNA-qPCR; both reliable to ~20 copies; LNA friendlier for clinical labs

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: SYBR Green detection (any assay)
rules.recommendation: Run a melting curve with every SYBR Green assay. Non-specific products (primer-dimer, off-target) are not visible in the Cq; the melting curve, or a gel, shows them.
pros: Detects primer-dimer and non-specific amplification products
Low cost — no probe required
cons: Adds analysis step
Cannot multiplex (single fluorescence channel)

sources.note: even LNA assays produced non-specific signal only revealed by melting curve

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: Multiplex or multi-target panel
rules.recommendation: For multiplex panels, consult stem-loop multiplex RT + dual-probe TaqMan literature. Primer cross-reactivity and probe spectral overlap must be verified empirically.
pros: Saves sample volume
Reduces cost and instrument time per target
Enables simultaneous normaliser co-amplification
cons: Primer/probe design complexity increases
May require optimisation of each primer pair concentration
Risk of competitive inhibition at high multiplex levels

sources.note: 21-miRNA multiplex stem-loop assay; cross-reactivity verification critical

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: Short or low-GC miRNA (edge E1 or E4)
rules.recommendation: For short (<18 nt) or low-GC (<30%) miRNAs, consider LNA substitution at 2-3 positions in the specific region, or extending the 5′ tail to raise forward primer Tm. Validate melting curve to confirm single-product amplification.
pros: LNA increases Tm by ~2-8°C per substitution for short targets [Andreasen10]
A longer 5′ tail raises the full-primer Tm (from PCR cycle 2 on) without changing the miRNA-specific region; it does not help cycle 1, where only that region binds
cons: LNA positions require empirical optimisation
Extended tails may increase primer-dimer risk — check structure_checks

sources.note: LNA spike for low-Tm miRNA targets
reliability at low copy number and difficult targets

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate experimentally before use in any diagnostic context.

rules.title: Clinical or diagnostic application
rules.recommendation: For clinical laboratory applications, LNA-qPCR may offer operational advantages (CAP/CLIA compatibility, kit-based workflow). Both stem-loop TaqMan and LNA-qPCR are analytically comparable at >20 copies per reaction.
pros: LNA-qPCR was used in a CAP/CLIA-compatible workflow [Kunwar23]
Stem-loop TaqMan is widely used since its description [Chen05]
cons: Regulatory validation (IVD) requires additional clinical studies beyond analytical performance
This tool is for research use only

sources.note: analytical validation of CogniMIR miRNA panel; LNA-qPCR clinically friendlier

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. NOT validated for clinical in-vitro diagnostic (IVD) use. Requires independent clinical validation.

rules.title: Multi-target normalization (reference gene selection)
rules.recommendation: Consider geNorm or NormFinder to select ≥2 stable reference miRNAs rather than a single U6 reference. For larger panels (≥10 targets, a threshold of this tool), global-mean normalization is an option that needs no candidate references; it assumes most miRNAs do not change. Reference stability depends on the sample type (Fujimoto 2018, Liang 2018).
pros: geNorm/NormFinder rank candidate references by stability in your data, which can reduce systematic bias [Hellemans14]
Global-mean normalization needs no prior reference selection (larger panels)
Reference choice depends on sample type: tissue ≠ plasma ≠ FFPE (Fujimoto 2018)
cons: geNorm requires ≥3 reference candidates — not feasible for very small panels
Global-mean assumes majority of miRNAs are unchanged — may not hold in disease states
Reference miRNA stability should be validated in your sample cohort before use

sources.note: geNorm normalization strategy for miRNA qPCR
Selecting 3 most stable miRNAs by multiple algorithms for normalization
Reference miRNA selection depends on sample type

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.

rules.title: Circulating miRNA (plasma/serum) — preanalytical QC + spike-in
rules.recommendation: For circulating miRNA in biofluids: (1) add cel-miR-39-3p spike-in before RNA extraction to correct for variable extraction efficiency; (2) assess hemolysis (miR-16/miR-451a ratio, McDonald 2011); (3) use one tube type for the whole study (EDTA vs serum changes the profile, Zhelankin 2022) and process every sample within the same short time window. Hemolysis can raise erythrocyte miRNAs (miR-92a, miR-451a) many-fold and mask the biofluid signal.
pros: cel-miR-39-3p spike-in can correct for variation in extraction efficiency [Tan15]
A hemolysis check (miR-16 / miR-451a) flags samples affected by erythrocyte miRNAs [McDonald11]
Tube type (EDTA vs serum) changes circulating miRNA yield and profile [Zhelankin22]; keep it constant
cons: The spike-in corrects extraction losses only if it is added before lysis/extraction
It does not correct for differences in sample input; use the same biofluid volume per extraction
The hemolysis check adds qPCR reactions per sample

sources.note: Spike-in normalization for serum/plasma miRNA; cel-miR-39 as exogenous control
Hemolysis alters plasma miRNA profile — miR-451a/miR-16 ratio as hemolysis marker
Anticoagulant tube type (EDTA vs serum) affects circulating miRNA yield and profile

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate preanalytical workflow for your sample type before quantification.

rules.title: Normalization — tissue / cell line: endogenous reference panel
rules.recommendation: Consider selecting ≥3 stable endogenous reference miRNAs with geNorm or NormFinder. Reference stability can differ between tissues; check it in your own cohort before quantification.
pros: geNorm/NormFinder rank candidate references by stability in your dataset [Hellemans14]
Several reference miRNAs can reduce normalization bias compared with one
cons: Requires a pilot experiment to identify stable references
Reference stability may differ between disease and healthy tissues

sources.note: geNorm normalization strategy for miRNA qPCR
Selecting 3 most stable miRNAs by multiple algorithms
Reference miRNA selection depends on sample type

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate reference stability in your sample type before quantification.

rules.title: Normalization — plasma / serum / biofluid: spike-in + global-mean
rules.recommendation: Add an exogenous cel-miR-39-3p spike-in before RNA extraction to correct for extraction efficiency. For larger panels (≥10 targets, a threshold of this tool), global-mean normalization is an option. Run a hemolysis check (miR-451a / miR-16) and consider excluding hemolyzed samples.
pros: cel-miR-39-3p spike-in can correct for variation in extraction efficiency [Tan15]
A hemolysis check flags samples affected by erythrocyte miRNAs [McDonald11]
cons: The spike-in corrects extraction losses only if it is added before lysis/extraction
Global-mean normalization needs a large enough panel (≥10 targets here, a tool threshold)

sources.note: Spike-in normalization for serum/plasma miRNA
Hemolysis alters plasma miRNA profile

rules.disclaimer: For research use only. Validate preanalytical workflow for your sample type.

rules.title: Normalization — FFPE / low-input: LNA-enhanced + stability validation
rules.recommendation: LNA-enhanced primers may improve sensitivity at low RNA input. Check reference miRNA stability in your own samples: extraction variability is typically higher in FFPE and low-input samples.
pros: LNA-enhanced primers raise Tm and hybridisation affinity [Andreasen10]
Several reference miRNAs can reduce the effect of extraction variability
cons: LNA synthesis is more expensive
Requires additional pilot experiments

sources.note: LNA-enhanced primer for degraded RNA
Reliability at low copy number

rules.title: Normalization — large panel (≥10 targets): global-mean normalization
rules.recommendation: For larger panels (≥10 targets, a threshold of this tool), global-mean normalization is an option that needs no pre-selected reference miRNAs. It assumes most miRNAs do not change between conditions.
pros: Needs no pre-selected reference miRNAs [Hellemans14]
Reduces bias from single reference gene instability
cons: Assumes majority of miRNAs unchanged — may not hold in highly dysregulated states
Not for small panels (<10 targets here)
